what_was_judged: Every in-bounds, non-weak_team, positioned detection on the 24 one-Hz frames
was rendered as a torso crop at 6x and looked at. A jersey number was recorded
only where it could be read with confidence; everything else is simply absent
Identity is (team, jersey). Both teams have a #28, so the jersey alone is not
an identity and the scorer must key on the pair.
caveats: These are the agent's own readings, not an independent human's.
**Legibility is far lower than the probe suggested and it is not uniform.**
The probe that justified this approach sampled frames 30, 105 and 180 and
found about half of crops readable. Over all 24 frames it is 52 of 241, about
22 %, and it tracks camera distance hard: the sheet covering f165-f210, where
the camera is closest, is around 50 % legible, while the sheets covering the
wide opening (f15-f105) and the wide ending (f270-f345) are nearer 12 %.
The consequence is stated rather than worked around: this measurement has good
sensitivity to an identity switch in the middle third of the possession and
poor sensitivity at either end. A switch during the opening or closing seconds
could go unseen. It is not evidence that none happened there.
**Three readings were withdrawn after scoring, and the mechanism that caught
them is worth keeping.** Two pairs of detections were read as the same number
on the same frame while being 6.1 and 23.5 yd apart - and two people cannot
wear one number. That is a consistency check the labels perform on themselves,
and it fired twice on 52 readings. Both pairs were re-rendered at 9x; neither
resolved, so all three readings involved were withdrawn rather than one of
each pair being picked. Withdrawing costs sensitivity; picking would have
invented a fact.
That also implies a reading error rate of very roughly 2 to 3 in 52 for the
readings that survive, since only conflicts that happen to collide on one
frame are detectable at all.

withdrawn_readings.why: conflicted with f30 #4, also read 5, 6.1 yd away - two different people cannot share a number. Re-rendered at 9x (ident_recheck.png): this one's number is half behind the player's arm and could be the 5 of a 51. Withdrawn rather than guessed.
conflicted with f180 #11, also read 51, 23.5 yd away. At 9x the second glyph could be a 1 or a 7 and I cannot tell which of the pair is wrong, so both are withdrawn.
the other half of the f180 conflict; see above.

Its slot, D7, was observed in every one of the 16 frames from f240 to f255 and never moved more than 0.3 yd between them. A continuously tracked slot moving sub-yard cannot have changed which person it holds, so a jersey change across that span had to be a reading error. That argument only chose which crop to re-examine; the decision came from the image, at 10x (d7_recheck.png): the second glyph is behind the player's arm and my reading was unreliable. Withdrawn rather than corrected to 28 - inferring 28 would use the tracker's own continuity, which is circular for a gate that measures the tracker.
